newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico 6-mos budget surplus 18.271 bln pesos-gov't.
newsitem.headline: Mexico 6-mos budget surplus 18.271 bln pesos-gov't.

text.p: Mexico said on Thursday it had registered a public sector budget surplus of 18.271 billion pesos in the first six months of 1997 -- 32.1 percent below that recorded in the first six months of last year.
A statement issued by the Finance Ministry also said that tax collection over the same period was up 11.1 percent against the year-ago period.
Other points in the Finance Ministry's end of second quarter statement of public sector finances and debt include:
- Total net public debt was 27.3 percent at the end of the second quarter, a decline of 1.2 percent from the end of March and down 3.0 percent from the end of 1996.
-- Net external public debt was $84.24 billion compared with $89.75 billion at the end of 1996.
-- Federal government net internal debt was 177.83 billion pesos at the end of June compared to 179.40 billion pesos at the end of 1996.

-- The Finance Ministry said the improved debt situation was the result of better public finances and a healthier external environment, which allowed the government to gradually improve the debt profile and reduce its borrowing costs.

-- The government said that in the first six months of 1997 it paid 15.0 centavos of each peso of its net bugetary spending in interest on the public debt, compared to 18.9 centavos it paid during 1996.
-- The government said the 18.27 billion peso public sector surplus in the first half of the year compared with a programmed deficit of 15.89 billion pesos for the full year.

-- It said the first half surplus was determined by three factors: better tax collection, a decline in debt servicing costs to 8.5 percent in real terms, and a 12.2 percent increase in real terms in primary spending.

-- The primary public surplus -- the difference between total income and spending excluding debt financing costs -- was 68.65 billion, a 19.5 percent decline in real terms compared to the same period last year.
-- Public sector revenues rose 4.5 percent in real terms to 335.199 billion pesos in the first half compared to the same period a year ago.

-- It said the gross external public sector debt -- federal government external debt, those companies under a federal budget and the development banks -- was $96.86 billion at the end of June. That was $2.93 billion higher than at the end of March this year.
-- In the second quarter, public sector external debt payments rose to $8.46 billion. Of that $6.46 billion was due to amortizing debt and $1.59 billion was used for servicing it, the statement said.
-- The balance of gross internal public debt was 214.18 billion pesos at the end of the second quarter, it said. That was 8.20 billion pesos higher than that seen on March 31, it added.
